findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced 10x without justification
findings.body: The global cleanup ticker is changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, so every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, and annotations) now runs 10x more often, not just annotation cleanup. This unrelated change increases DB and filesystem load on all Grafana instances and partially works against the goal of reducing MySQL contention from annotation cleanup. It should be reverted or justified and scoped to annotations only.

findings.title: Routine cleanup progress is logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log 'Annotations/Tags to clean' and 'cleaned ...' via r.log.Error on every batch, including successful batches where err is nil. This will emit error-level logs (often wired to alerting/error reporting) for normal operation and each message embeds the full ids slice, which can be tens of thousands of IDs for large batch sizes, creating huge noisy log lines. These should be Debug/Info level without dumping all IDs.

findings.title: SQLite inline ID list is built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: For SQLite with a large batch size, deleteByIDs builds the IN (...) list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop over all ids. Each iteration copies the entire accumulated string, so building a 32767-ID list (as exercised by the new test) is O(n^2) in bytes copied and can take seconds and large allocations before the DELETE runs. Use strings.Builder (already imported) to build the list linearly.
